greek_hesiod_hyperion.name: Watches from on high over the celestial light
greek_hesiod_hyperion.notes: As the light-Titan whose name means 'he who goes/watches above,' he governs heavenly illumination.

greek_hesiod_hyperion.name: Sires the Sun, Moon and Dawn upon Theia
greek_hesiod_hyperion.notes: By Theia (Euryphaessa) he is generative source of Helios, Selene and Eos.

sources.reference: Hesiod, Theogony; Homeric Hymn 31 to Helios

greek_hesiod_theia.name: Bestows radiance and the value of bright gold
greek_hesiod_theia.notes: Pindar invokes 'Theia of many names,' saying that for her sake mortals honour gold as mightiest and prize the worth she lends to contending ships and chariot-teams.

greek_hesiod_iapetus.name: Progenitor of mankind through his sons
greek_hesiod_iapetus.notes: Through Atlas, Menoetius, Prometheus and Epimetheus his line is bound up with the human lot and its defining traits.

greek_hesiod_menoetius.name: Embodies insolent might and reckless presumption
greek_hesiod_menoetius.notes: Defined by overweening violence and pride; for his atasthalia and overbearing manhood Zeus struck him with a smoking thunderbolt and hurled him to Erebos.

greek_hesiod_phoebe.name: Holds and bestows the Delphic oracle
greek_hesiod_phoebe.notes: In the Eumenides prologue Phoebe receives the Delphic seat from Themis and gives it to Apollo as a birth-gift; Apollo is called Phoibos after her.

greek_hesiod_oceanus.name: Primeval source from whom the gods and all waters spring
greek_hesiod_oceanus.notes: Homer's Hera calls him 'Oceanus, origin of the gods'; as the world-encircling stream he is wellspring of every river, spring and sea.

greek_hesiod_tethys.name: Nurses and nurtures the divine generation
greek_hesiod_tethys.notes: In Iliad 14 Hera says Tethys reared her in her halls during the Titanomachy; her name evokes the nurse/grandmother.

greek_hesiod_pallas_titan.name: Sires the war-powers Nike, Kratos, Bia and Zelos upon Styx
greek_hesiod_pallas_titan.notes: By Styx he fathers Victory, Strength, Force and Emulation, the warlike personifications who thereafter dwell beside Zeus.

greek_hesiod_styx.name: Her water is the gods' inviolable oath
greek_hesiod_styx.notes: A god who forswears by Styx-water lies breathless and speechless a great year, cut off from nectar and ambrosia, then is banished nine years from the council of the gods.

greek_hesiod_styx.name: First to bring aid to Zeus in the Titanomachy
greek_hesiod_styx.notes: On her father's counsel she came first, bringing her children to Zeus; in reward Zeus made her the great oath of the gods and kept her children ever at his side.

greek_hesiod_styx.name: Her cold water is deadly to mortals and beasts
greek_hesiod_styx.notes: The Arcadian Styx that trickles down the cliff near Nonacris was reputed death to men and animals and to corrode most materials.

greek_hesiod_nyx.name: Gives oracles consulted even by Zeus
greek_hesiod_nyx.notes: In the Orphic theogony Nyx, immortal nurse of the gods, sits in her cave knowing all oracles; Zeus comes to her and she prophesies how he will found his rule.

greek_hesiod_nyx.name: Commands awe from Zeus himself
greek_hesiod_nyx.notes: In Iliad 14 Zeus shrinks from doing what would displease swift Night, who subdues gods and men, and so spares Hypnos.

greek_hesiod_hypnos.name: Can lull even Zeus and Ocean to sleep
greek_hesiod_hypnos.notes: At Hera's bidding he put Zeus to sleep on Mt Ida (and once before, during the Heracles episode), boasting he could lull all gods and even the streams of Okeanos.

greek_hesiod_hypnos.name: Bears away the dead with his twin Death
greek_hesiod_hypnos.notes: With Thanatos he carries the body of Sarpedon from Troy to be laid to rest in Lycia.

greek_hesiod_thanatos.name: Hallows the dying by cutting a lock of hair
greek_hesiod_thanatos.notes: In Euripides' Alcestis Thanatos comes with his sword to shear a lock of the victim's hair, consecrating her to the gods below.

greek_hesiod_thanatos.name: Can be bound or wrestled down
greek_hesiod_thanatos.notes: Sisyphus chained Death so that none died until Ares freed him; Heracles ambushed and wrestled Thanatos at the tomb to win back Alcestis.

greek_hesiod_leto.name: Gentle protectress and nurturer of the young
greek_hesiod_leto.notes: Hesiod calls her always mild and kindliest within Olympos; she is patroness of children and mothers.

greek_hesiod_leto.name: Avenges insult to her honour through her children
greek_hesiod_leto.notes: Apollo and Artemis slew the Niobids when Niobe vaunted over Leto, and destroyed the giant Tityos for his assault upon her.

sources.reference: Homer, Iliad; Homer, Odyssey 11; Apollodorus, Bibliotheca

greek_hesiod_mnemosyne.name: Personifies Memory, wellspring of inspired song
greek_hesiod_mnemosyne.notes: Through her daughters the Muses she grants kings and bards their authoritative speech and a forgetting of sorrows.

greek_hesiod_mnemosyne.name: Presides over the Spring of Memory in the afterlife
greek_hesiod_mnemosyne.notes: The Orphic-Bacchic gold tablets bid the soul drink not from Lethe but from the cold Lake of Mnemosyne, to keep memory and escape rebirth.

greek_hesiod_themis.name: Convenes and regulates the assembly of the gods
greek_hesiod_themis.notes: At Zeus's command she summons the gods to council and, when Hera returns to Olympos, hands her the welcome-cup.

greek_hesiod_themis.name: Holds the Delphic oracle and counsels Zeus
greek_hesiod_themis.notes: She held Delphi in succession after Gaia and before Phoebe, and warned Zeus that Thetis would bear a son greater than his father.

greek_hesiod_uranus.name: Shelters and covers Earth on every side
greek_hesiod_uranus.notes: Gaia bore him equal to herself that he might envelop her wholly as the all-covering sky.

greek_hesiod_thaumas.name: Sires the rainbow Iris and the storm-Harpies
greek_hesiod_thaumas.notes: By the Oceanid Electra he fathers swift Iris (the rainbow) and the long-haired Harpies Aello and Ocypete, marvels of sky and sea.

greek_hesiod_selene.name: Gives light by night, her radiance wheeling round the earth
greek_hesiod_selene.notes: Bathed in Ocean and clad in far-gleaming raiment she yokes her bright team, and the glow from her immortal head encircles the earth.

greek_hesiod_selene.name: Measures out the months
greek_hesiod_selene.notes: Her fifty daughters by Endymion, the Menai, were reckoned the fifty lunar months of the four-year Olympiad.

greek_iasion.name: Founds and teaches the Samothracian Mysteries
greek_iasion.notes: Zeus taught Iasion the rites of the Great Gods of Samothrace, and he was first to initiate strangers, raising the mysteries to high repute.

greek_iasion.name: Begets agricultural Wealth on Demeter
greek_iasion.notes: Lying with Demeter in a thrice-ploughed field he fathered Plutus (Wealth), the wealth of the corn; for the union Zeus struck him with a thunderbolt.

greek_iamus.name: Divines from the burnt offerings on the altar of Zeus
greek_iamus.notes: After Heracles founded the Olympic Games Apollo granted Iamus the right to prophesy from the altar-fire at Olympia, where his clan officiated.

greek_idmon.name: Foreknew his own death yet sailed regardless
greek_idmon.notes: By his Apolline mantic art he knew he was fated to die on the voyage, yet joined the Argo rather than deny it glory.

greek_io.name: Priestess of Hera at the Argive Heraion
greek_io.notes: She served Hera at Argos when Zeus's desire fell upon her, the office that frames her whole tragedy.

greek_io.name: Foremother of the Danaid and Heraclid lineage
greek_io.notes: Restored in Egypt by Zeus's touch she bore Epaphus, ancestor of the Danaids and ultimately of Heracles.

greek_ion_athens.name: Organizes the four Ionian tribes
greek_ion_athens.notes: He named the Geleontes, Hopletes, Argadeis and Aigikoreis after his sons, the ancestral Ionian tribal divisions.

sources.reference: Euripides, Ion; Pausanias, Description of Greece 7.1

greek_ion_athens.name: Leads Athens as war-commander against Eleusis
greek_ion_athens.notes: Invited by the Athenians, he commanded them in the war against Eleusis and was honoured as polemarch.

greek_hesiod_styx.name: Ewer of Styx-water for the oath
greek_hesiod_styx.notes: The pitcher of the river's water that Iris fetches so a swearing god may pour it out while taking the great oath.

greek_hesiod_hypnos.name: Poppy of sleep
greek_hesiod_hypnos.notes: Opium-poppy stalk borne as the giver of sleep, with a horn from which slumber is poured.

greek_hesiod_hypnos.name: Horn pouring out sleep
greek_hesiod_hypnos.notes: In iconography he pours soporific slumber from a horn over the heads of gods and men.

greek_hesiod_leto.name: Date-palm of Delos
greek_hesiod_leto.notes: The palm by the streams of Inopos against which she leaned in her labour with Apollo.

greek_hesiod_rhea.name: Swaddled stone given to Cronus
greek_hesiod_rhea.notes: The stone wrapped in swaddling-clothes she gave Cronus to swallow in place of the infant Zeus; later set up as the Omphalos at Delphi.

sources.reference: Hesiod, Theogony; Pausanias, Description of Greece (Phocis)

greek_hesiod_rhea.name: Tympanum (hand-drum)
greek_hesiod_rhea.notes: As Meter, Mother of the Gods, she rejoices in the rattle of castanets and beat of drums in her ecstatic rites.

sources.reference: Homeric Hymn 14 to the Mother of the Gods; Orphic Hymn to Rhea

greek_hesiod_rhea.name: Lion-drawn chariot
greek_hesiod_rhea.notes: As Cybele/Meter she drives a holy car drawn by fierce lions.

greek_hesiod_themis.name: Scales of judgement
greek_hesiod_themis.notes: The cult-statue at Rhamnous (c. 300 BCE) held scales in one hand and an offering-bowl in the other; the blindfold of later Justice is post-classical.

greek_hesiod_selene.name: Crescent moon
greek_hesiod_selene.notes: Worn on the brow or rising behind the shoulders like horns, her defining emblem in art.

greek_hesiod_selene.name: Torch
greek_hesiod_selene.notes: Carried as bringer of light through the night.

greek_hesione.name: Veil given as ransom for Podarces
greek_hesione.notes: The veil she took from her head and gave to ransom her brother, who was thereafter called Priam ('the ransomed').

greek_iphigenia.name: Wooden image of Artemis from Tauris
greek_iphigenia.notes: The cult-statue she and Orestes carry off from the Taurians and bring to Halae and Brauron in Attica.

greek_ion_athens.name: Woven cradle of his exposure
greek_ion_athens.notes: The round basket-cradle with its swaddling clothes in which he was exposed, the chief recognition-token in Euripides' Ion.

sources.reference: Hesiod, Theogony (golden-crowned Phoebe); later lunar association
Homeric Hymn 14 to the Mother of the Gods
Hesiod, Theogony; Diodorus Siculus, Library of History
Pausanias, Description of Greece; Strabo, Geography
Homeric Hymn 14; Orphic Hymn to Rhea

greek_hesiod_styx.gloss: the great oath of the gods

greek_hesiod_nyx.name: Oracle of Night at Megara
greek_hesiod_nyx.notes: On the Megarian acropolis (Karia) Pausanias records an oracle of Night, beside sanctuaries of Dionysos Nyktelios and Aphrodite Epistrophia.

greek_hesiod_hypnos.name: Sanctuary of Sleep with the Muses at Troezen
greek_hesiod_hypnos.notes: At Troezen Hypnos was honoured together with the Muses; Pausanias also notes a statue of Sleep in an Asclepian healing context.

greek_hesiod_leto.name: Cult of Leto on Delos
greek_hesiod_leto.notes: At her birth-sanctuary on Delos Leto was honoured with Apollo and Artemis in choral and athletic contests.

greek_hesiod_leto.name: Cult of Leto Phytie at Phaistos (Ekdysia)
greek_hesiod_leto.notes: At Phaistos in Crete Leto Phytie ('the Grafter') was honoured at the Ekdysia ('the Stripping'), commemorating the change of Leukippos from maid to youth.

greek_hesiod_leto.name: The Letoon of Lycia
greek_hesiod_leto.notes: Near Xanthos the Letoon was the federal sanctuary of the Lycians, where Leto was effectively the national tutelary goddess.

greek_hesiod_mnemosyne.name: Spring of Mnemosyne at the oracle of Trophonios
greek_hesiod_mnemosyne.notes: At Lebadeia the inquirer drank from Lethe to forget former cares, then from the spring of Mnemosyne to remember the vision, and was seated on the chair of Memory to recount it.

greek_hesiod_rhea.name: Cretan cult of the infant Zeus with the Kouretes
greek_hesiod_rhea.notes: On Crete (Mt Ida/Dikte) the armed Kouretes clashed shields to drown the cries of the hidden infant Zeus; Rhea's worship there merged with the Phrygian Meter/Cybele cult of drums, flutes and lions.

greek_hesiod_themis.name: Cult of Themis at Rhamnous beside Nemesis
greek_hesiod_themis.notes: At Rhamnous in Attica Themis was worshipped beside Nemesis; a dedication by Megakles and a cult-statue (c. 300 BCE) survive. Pausanias also records an altar of Themis at Olympia and a sanctuary at Thebes.

greek_hyacinthus.name: The Hyacinthia at Amyclae
greek_hyacinthus.notes: The second great Spartan festival, turning from mourning for Hyacinthus to rejoicing for Apollo; his tomb-altar lay beneath the colossal Throne of Apollo at the Amyclaeum, with offerings made through a bronze door.

greek_hippodamia.name: Sacrifices to Hippodamia in the Hippodameion at Olympia
greek_hippodamia.notes: A walled precinct in the Altis which women entered once a year to sacrifice to Hippodamia; her bones were said to have been brought to Olympia by oracle. She also founded the Heraia maidens' footrace in gratitude to Hera.

greek_hilaeira.name: Sanctuary of Hilaeira and Phoebe at Sparta
greek_hilaeira.notes: The Leucippides Hilaeira and Phoebe shared a Spartan sanctuary served by maiden priestesses themselves called the Leukippides; a priestess once renewed the face of one cult-image but was warned in a dream not to touch the other.

greek_homer_tlepolemus.name: Hero-cult and games of Tlepolemus at Rhodes
greek_homer_tlepolemus.notes: At Rhodes Tlepolemus received hero-honours with processions and burnt sacrifices of flocks and athletic games, the contests at which Diagoras of Rhodes won.

greek_idmon.name: Hero-cult of Idmon at Heraclea Pontica
greek_idmon.notes: Slain by a boar in Mariandynian land, Idmon was buried there; the Delphic oracle later bade the colonists of Heraclea Pontica build their city around his tomb and worship him as guardian hero.

greek_iamus.name: Hereditary mantic priesthood of the Iamidai at Olympia
greek_iamus.notes: Iamus' descendants, the Iamidai, were the hereditary seers officiating at the great altar of Zeus at Olympia (and elsewhere, e.g. Sparta) into historical times.

greek_iphigenia.name: Cult of Iphigenia at Brauron and Halae (Artemis Tauropolos/Brauronia)
greek_iphigenia.notes: At Brauron she was honoured in the sanctuary of Artemis (offerings of the clothes of women who died in childbirth dedicated to her); at Halae Araphenides the cult of Artemis Tauropolos kept a token blood-rite recalling Taurian sacrifice. Megara also claimed her tomb.

sources.reference: Euripides, Iphigenia in Tauris; Pausanias, Description of Greece (Attica)

greek_iasion.name: The Samothracian Mysteries of the Great Gods
greek_iasion.notes: Iasion figures as founder within the Mysteries of the Great Gods (Cabeiri) of Samothrace, which he was first to open to strangers.

greek_io.name: Identification with Isis in Egypt
greek_io.notes: In Egypt Io was identified with the cow-formed goddess Isis, and her son Epaphus with the bull Apis; the Ionian Sea and the Bosporus ('ox-ford') were named from her wanderings.

greek_ion_athens.name: Hero-tomb of Ion at Potamoi in Attica
greek_ion_athens.notes: Ion died in Attica and his tomb stood in the deme of Potamoi; he was honoured as eponymous ancestor of the Ionians.

attributes.name: Bull-horns at the temples
attributes.notes: Depicted as an aged bearded man with bull's horns (and sometimes crab-claw horns) sprouting from his brow, after the Greek convention of rivers as bull-formed.

attributes.name: Serpentine fish-tailed body
attributes.notes: From the Hellenistic period shown with a coiling fish-tailed lower body, reclining as a river-god with urn, oar and attendant sea-creatures.

attributes.name: Dark star-spangled mantle
attributes.notes: Robed in dark mist or a starry veil, she drives a horse-drawn chariot across the sky from the ends of the earth.

attributes.name: Bearing the infant twins Sleep and Death
attributes.notes: On the Chest of Cypselus, Pausanias reports, Night is shown carrying the two boys Sleep and Death, the one white, the other black.

attributes.name: Wings at the temples
attributes.notes: A gentle winged youth, sometimes shown with wings springing from his brow or shoulders.

attributes.name: Winged, black-clad figure
attributes.notes: A winged figure, in Euripides dressed in black and bearing a sword; in funerary art often with an inverted, extinguished torch.

attributes.name: Heart of iron
attributes.notes: Hesiod gives Death a pitiless heart of iron and a spirit of bronze, hateful even to the gods.

attributes.name: Veiled matron
attributes.notes: Depicted as a mantled, modest matron, in keeping with her mild and demure character.

sacredAnimals.name: Wolf
sacredAnimals.notes: Wolves are linked to her in the aetiology of her coming from the Hyperboreans and her arrival in Lycia.

attributes.name: Enthroned with mural crown
attributes.notes: As Meter/Cybele she is enthroned, wearing a turreted crown, holding a tympanum and phiale, flanked by lions or riding a lion-drawn car.

sources.reference: Homeric Hymn 14 to the Mother of the Gods; Orphic Hymn to Rhea

attributes.name: Billowing veil arched over the head
attributes.notes: A flowing mantle and veil arch over her head like a night-sky halo, the crescent at her brow, as she drives a two-horse biga.

attributes.name: Horned cult-image at Elis
attributes.notes: Pausanias saw a stone image of a horned Selene in the agora at Elis, and a relief of Selene driving on the base of the Zeus at Olympia.

sacredAnimals.name: Bull / ox
sacredAnimals.notes: Oxen sometimes draw her car, paralleling the bull-horn moon imagery.

attributes.name: Carried up to heaven on the Throne of Apollo
attributes.notes: On the Throne of Apollo at Amyclae, made by Bathycles, Hyacinthus and his sister Polyboea were shown being borne up to heaven by gods.

sacredPlants.name: Hyacinth flower
sacredPlants.notes: Sprang from his blood, its petals marked with the mourning cry AI AI.

attributes.name: Horned maiden / white heifer
attributes.notes: Shown as a horned maiden or a white cow, watched by the many-eyed Argus Panoptes and stung onward by Hera's gadfly.

sacredAnimals.name: Gadfly
sacredAnimals.notes: The oistros sent by Hera that drives her over the world.

attributes.name: At the altar with the substituted deer
attributes.notes: The canonical scene shows her at the altar of Aulis with the sacrificial knife, and the deer set in her place by Artemis.
